# SharkSight on one cloud VM (D-061): the two app containers (db, app) plus a small HTTPS + password proxy.
# Provider-neutral; deploy/aws/deploy.sh puts it on an EC2 instance. Secrets come from .env next to this file
# (generated by the script, 0600). Sized for a small VM (2 GB RAM + 2 GB swap): Postgres is tuned small.
name: sharksight

services:
  db:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:0.8.0-pg17
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: sharksight
      POSTGRES_DB: sharksight
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?}
      # byte/code-point text order, exactly like the local database (D-059)
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: "--encoding=UTF8 --locale-provider=builtin --builtin-locale=C.UTF-8 --locale=C.UTF-8"
    command: ["postgres", "-c", "shared_buffers=64MB", "-c", "work_mem=8MB", "-c", "maintenance_work_mem=64MB",
              "-c", "max_connections=30"]
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./restore:/restore:ro
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${DB_HOST_PORT:-5432}:5432"     # VM-local only (no firewall rule): reach it through `deploy.sh tunnel`
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U sharksight -d sharksight"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30
    restart: unless-stopped

  app:
    image: ${APP_IMAGE:-sharksight:prod-arm64}
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      APP_ENV: production
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://sharksight_app:${APP_DB_PASSWORD:REDACTED
      MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://sharksight:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:REDACTED
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data          # settings.json (API key, limits, agent settings) and the 3D models
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${APP_HOST_PORT:-8600}:8600"     # VM-local only: the proxy (or an SSH tunnel) is the way in
    depends_on:
      db: { condition: service_healthy }
    restart: unless-stopped

  proxy:
    image: caddy:2.10-alpine
    profiles: [public]            # deploy.sh starts it unless --private
    env_file: .env                # SITE_ADDRESS, BASIC_AUTH_USER, BASIC_AUTH_HASH
    ports:
      - "${HTTP_PORT:-80}:80"
      - "${HTTPS_PORT:-443}:443"
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy_data:/data
    depends_on: [app]
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  pgdata:
  caddy_data:
# HTTPS (Let's Encrypt for <ip>.sslip.io, or your own domain) and one password in front of the app, which has no login
# of its own yet. Set by deploy.sh in .env: SITE_ADDRESS, BASIC_AUTH_USER, BASIC_AUTH_HASH (bcrypt).
{$SITE_ADDRESS} {
	encode zstd gzip
	basic_auth {
		{$BASIC_AUTH_USER} {$BASIC_AUTH_HASH}
	}
	reverse_proxy app:8600
}

# Deploying SharkSight to AWS (D-061)

One EC2 instance runs the same containers as your laptop: **db** (PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector), **app** (API + the built
PM app) and a small **proxy** (Caddy: HTTPS + one password, because the app has no login of its own yet).

```
deploy/compose.yaml   the stack on the instance (provider-neutral)
deploy/Caddyfile      HTTPS for <ip>.sslip.io + basic auth in front of the app
deploy/aws/deploy.sh  the CLI: create the instance, ship the image and files, start, copy data, tunnel, destroy
```

## Cost

Made for the **AWS Free plan** (accounts since 2025-07-15): $100 credits at sign-up, up to $100 more for trying
five services, valid 6 months; when credits or time run out the account closes instead of billing you — as long as
you stay on the Free plan (don't upgrade to Paid). Rough use of the credits (eu-central-1, check the AWS pricing
calculator): t4g.small ≈ $14 / month, 20 GB gp3 ≈ $2, public IPv4 ≈ $3.65 → about $20 / month, so the credits last
the 6 months. `deploy.sh budget you@example.com` adds a $5 cost alarm (and earns one of the $20 credit activities).

## One-time setup (you)

1. Create an AWS account and choose the **Free plan**.
2. In the console, create an IAM user for yourself (not the root user) with access keys, or set up IAM Identity Center.
3. On this Mac: `brew install awscli`, then `aws configure` (keys, region `eu-central-1`) or `aws configure sso`.
4. `deploy/aws/deploy.sh check`

## Deploy

```bash
deploy/aws/deploy.sh create          # key pair, security group, t4g.small (Ubuntu 24.04 ARM); wait ~2 min for Docker
deploy/aws/deploy.sh deploy          # build the ARM image, send it + compose + .env + settings + 3D models, start
deploy/aws/deploy.sh data            # copy your local database into the instance (once; --replace to overwrite)
deploy/aws/deploy.sh url             # https://<ip>.sslip.io — user pm, password in deploy/aws/.env.vm
deploy/aws/deploy.sh budget you@example.com
```

After a code change: `deploy/aws/deploy.sh deploy` again (data stays; the app migrates the schema on start).

## Day to day

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status`, `logs`, `ssh` | container state, last 200 log lines, a shell on the instance |
| `tunnel` | app on http://127.0.0.1:8601 and the instance's Postgres on 127.0.0.1:5434 — e.g. run a pipeline stage from this Mac against the cloud database with `DATABASE_URL=REDACTED` |
| `up --private` | db + app only, no public proxy; use `tunnel` to reach it |
| `allow-my-ip` | your IP changed and SSH is refused |
| `stop` / `start` | pause the instance (disk and data stay; the public IP changes → `push` then `up`) |
| `destroy` | terminate the instance and delete its disk (all cloud data), security group and key pair |

## What is where

- Secrets: `deploy/aws/.env.vm` (generated from your `.env`: OpenAI key, database passwords, the web login) and the SSH
  key `deploy/aws/sharksight.pem` — both git-ignored, 0600. On the instance they are `~/sharksight/.env`.
- Ports: only 80/443 (proxy) are open to the world, SSH only from your IP; the app (8600) and Postgres (5432) listen on
  the instance's localhost.
- `deploy.sh` with `DEPLOY_TARGET=local` runs every step against a directory on this Mac instead of the instance
  (project `sharksight-vmtest`, ports 8088 / 8602 / 5435) — that is how the flow was tested.

## Before anyone else uses it

The proxy password is shared, so the audit trail still records whatever name the browser sends (`X-Actor`). Real
logins for people, app settings in the database instead of `data/settings.json`, and the 3D models in S3 are the next
steps for a proper deployment (STATE → Next up).

# Deploying SharkSight to Google Cloud (D-062)

One Compute Engine VM runs the same containers as your laptop: **db** (PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector), **app** (API + the
built PM app) and a small **proxy** (Caddy: HTTPS + one password, because the app has no login of its own yet).

```
deploy/compose.yaml   the stack on the VM (provider-neutral)
deploy/Caddyfile      HTTPS for <ip>.sslip.io + basic auth in front of the app
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh  the CLI: create the VM, ship the image and files, start, copy data, tunnel, destroy
deploy/aws/deploy.sh  the same for one AWS EC2 instance (D-061, not used: Atahan dropped AWS)
```

## Cost

Made for the **Google Cloud free tier**: one e2-micro VM (2 shared vCPUs, 1 GB RAM) and 30 GB of standard disk are
free every month in `us-west1`, `us-central1` or `us-east1`, plus 1 GB of outbound traffic. A public IPv4 address may
be billed (a few dollars a month). New accounts also get a **$300 / 90-day trial credit**; as long as you don't
upgrade to a paid account, nothing is charged when it runs out. `deploy.sh budget` adds a $5 monthly alert.

1 GB is tight for Postgres + the app: the VM gets 2 GB of swap and Postgres is tuned small. If it is too slow,
`MACHINE_TYPE=e2-small` (2 GB, ≈ $12 / month, from the trial credit) — `destroy`, then `create` with it.

## One-time setup (you)

1. Create a Google Cloud account at https://console.cloud.google.com (card needed for verification; trial credit).
2. Create a project (e.g. `sharksight`) and make sure billing is linked to it.
3. On this Mac: `brew install --cask google-cloud-sdk`, then `gcloud auth login` and
   `gcloud config set project <project-id>`.
4. `deploy/gcp/deploy.sh check` (also switches on the Compute Engine API)

## Deploy

```bash
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh create          # SSH key, network + firewall, e2-micro (Ubuntu 24.04); wait ~2 min for Docker
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh deploy          # build the x86 image, send it + compose + .env + settings + 3D models, start
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh data            # copy your local database into the VM (once; --replace to overwrite)
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh url             # https://<ip>.sslip.io — user pm, password in deploy/gcp/.env.vm
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh budget
```

After a code change: `deploy/gcp/deploy.sh deploy` again (data stays; the app migrates the schema on start).

## Day to day

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status`, `logs`, `ssh` | container state, last 200 log lines, a shell on the VM |
| `tunnel` | app on http://127.0.0.1:8601 and the VM's Postgres on 127.0.0.1:5434 — e.g. run a pipeline stage from this Mac against the cloud database with `DATABASE_URL=REDACTED` |
| `up --private` | db + app only, no public proxy; use `tunnel` to reach it |
| `allow-my-ip` | your IP changed and SSH is refused |
| `stop` / `start` | pause the VM (disk and data stay; the public IP changes → `push` then `up`) |
| `destroy` | delete the VM and its disk (all cloud data), firewall rules, network and SSH key |

Settings: `GCP_PROJECT` (default: gcloud's current project), `GCP_ZONE` (`us-central1-a`), `MACHINE_TYPE` (`e2-micro`).

## What is where

- Secrets: `deploy/gcp/.env.vm` (generated from your `.env`: OpenAI key, database passwords, the web login) and the SSH
  key `deploy/gcp/sharksight.key` — both git-ignored, 0600. On the VM they are `~sharksight/sharksight/.env`.
- Ports: the VM has its own network `sharksight` (not the default one, which allows SSH from anywhere): only 80/443
  (proxy) are open to the world, SSH only from your IP; the app (8600) and Postgres (5432) listen on the VM's localhost.
- The image is built for linux/amd64; on an ARM Mac the Python part is emulated (the frontend builds natively).

## Before anyone else uses it

The proxy password is shared, so the audit trail still records whatever name the browser sends (`X-Actor`). Real
logins for people, app settings in the database instead of `data/settings.json`, and the 3D models in object storage
are the next steps for a proper deployment (STATE → Next up).

**What you need to do first:**
1. Create a Google Cloud account at console.cloud.google.com. New accounts get a $300 credit for 90 days, and nothing is charged afterwards unless you upgrade to a paid account. Then create a project and make sure billing is linked to it.

**Then deploy:**
```
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh check     # also switches on the Compute Engine API
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh create    # creates the server; wait ~2 min for Docker to install

# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

## Platform

web

## Stack

React + TypeScript (Vite) frontend with three.js via react-three-fiber for real-time 3D; a small FastAPI JSON layer (`backend/src/api/`) over the existing Python pipeline (`backend/src/bmw_req`, PostgreSQL + pgvector, D-059). Chosen by Atahan on 2026-10-11 to replace the Streamlit UI (D-039). Runs locally only (confidential BMW data, AGENTS rule 1).

## Users

- **Primary: a BMW product manager (PM)** responsible for what the successor of a car line (1, 5, 7 Series) offers its customers in each market. Over a ~2-year process they review AI-drafted customer requirements, decide (approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge, always with a reason), set priorities per car × market, and hand the result to engineering — while new evidence keeps arriving.
- **Demo audience: BMW judges and mentors** of the "AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon, watching the PM (Atahan) work the tool live on a laptop or projector. The UI is tuned demo-first: the story must land in a few clicks, without breaking the real tool underneath.

## Product Purpose

Turn ~10k customer comments, a customer study, sales data, option lists and cited web research into prioritized, evidence-linked customer requirements for successor BMW cars, per car and market. The AI reads, groups, drafts, checks fit and scores; the PM decides; everything is traceable to the customer's words and audited. Success: a PM trusts and acts on the ranking because every number explains itself, and the judges see a living decision process, not a one-shot list.

## Positioning

Not a feedback dashboard and not a chatbot: a decision instrument. Every requirement is a product decision BMW could take or trade off, scored per market with a visible factor breakdown, traced down to individual comments, gated by brand fit, and re-proposed — never silently changed — as new evidence arrives in waves.

## Operating Context

- Simulated ~2-year process: three evidence waves (feedback has no dates), each re-scoring and producing AI change proposals the PM accepts or rejects.
- Portfolio: F70 (1 Series), G60 (5 Series), G68 (5 Series LWB, China), G70 (7 Series); markets USA, Europe, China, Rest of world.
- Hand-offs: defect-type pain goes to a Quality hand-over list, not into requirements; the approved list is exported.
- Today's car matters as a reference: the current car and its equipment (German price list; public BMW configurator) are the baseline the successor improves on.

## Capabilities and Constraints

- AI only proposes; approved/rejected/deferred need a named human and a rationale. Brand-fit FAIL blocks approval unless the PM overrides with a reason. Audit is append-only.
- Scope: customer-facing requirements only — no regulatory, engineering specs or pricing.
- Evidence and assumption are always shown apart; conflicting evidence is surfaced, not hidden; markets without own comments are labelled.
- OpenAI is the only LLM provider; $100 total budget; running a wave costs money and takes minutes.
- Terminology to keep (English): Must / Should / Could; "5 Series · USA"; Strong / Good / Limited evidence / Assumption only; Expected / Differentiator / Delighter; To review / Challenged / Approved / Deferred / Rejected; "AI suggests" for unconfirmed priorities.
- A parallel workstream (D-040+) adds requirement origins (competitors, trends, regulation, personas), a regulatory radar, customer & model groups, an offering matrix per market and market intelligence; the IA must have a home for these.

## Brand Commitments

- English UI, current domain terms.
- Dark theme only.
- A BMW-like blue accent is wanted.
- No BMW logo or trademark branding in the UI; neutral product name.

## Evidence on Hand

- Live database (PostgreSQL in Docker): 10,128 verbatims, 1,369 cited research / web / reference items, study metrics, sales, option lists; 15,440 classified signals; 76 (JAN 26) / 80 (JUL 26) requirements and 252 / 259 prioritized line × market targets; ~2.9k audit events. Verbatims are BMW-confidential: localhost only.
- 3D models of today's cars: public CC BY Sketchfab models (attribution required), downloaded by Atahan into `data/models/` (Q-025). Fan-made approximations, not BMW CAD.
- No testimonials, user research or production usage exist — never fabricate them.

## Product Principles

1. The PM decides, the AI explains — every AI output is a proposal with its cause visible.
2. One number, fully opened — any score can be unfolded to its factors and down to the customer's words.
3. Markets are different customers — never average them away; show where they disagree.
4. The car is the canvas — requirements are about a physical product; show them on it.
5. A process, not a report — what changed since last time comes first.

Moved here on 2026-10-13 at Atahan's request: this repo stays lean and covers the BMW requirements app as it is.
Everything below is vision or future work that will be picked up **in another repo**. Nothing here is a commitment;
agents working in this repo don't act on it. The IDs Q-027 / Q-028 are kept so older decisions that cite them

## 1. A domain-agnostic SharkSight (was Q-028, open)

- Owner: Atahan · raised 2026-10-12
- Atahan is considering a version anyone can use for ground-up requirements engineering and product decisions.
  Market scan: artifact https://claude.ai/artifact/RPFgwBDcz8TFr46pbhLJYA (feedback intelligence, PM suites, RM/ALM,
  AI-native systems engineering, CI, preference research). Finding: no tool covers evidence → measurable requirements →
  gated, per-segment priority → human decision → audit; closest are Productboard Spark upstream and Flow Engineering
  downstream.
- Open: positioning (a layer between VoC tools and RM/ALM tools?), beachhead (long-cycle physical products?), what
  becomes config (org / product line / segment, pluggable gates, generic ingest, optional 3D visualizer), integrations
  (Jira, Jama/Polarion, ReqIF, MCP), and how the BMW-specific rules (brand fit, plant/platform feasibility) map to
  generic gates.
- 2026-10-12 — Method packs + evidence depth (Scrum, Kanban, OKR, SAFe, discovery, stage-gate): artifact
  https://claude.ai/artifact/MMKqm5c2NihxE8uwGBu1SQ. Key point: evidence depth should scale with decision cost /
  reversibility (light / medium / deep); stories inherit evidence from their epic or opportunity; agile evidence comes
  mostly after the decision (outcome measurement). Proposal only.

## 2. Continuous data intake instead of fixed checkpoints (was Q-027, open)

- Owner: Atahan · raised 2026-10-11
- The two fixed checkpoints (D-040) would eventually go; new data gets digested automatically — e.g. a background agent
  that searches the web from time to time, and users uploading new data into the knowledge base.
- Open: how evidence is versioned without checkpoints (rolling snapshots? event time?), what a "run" is then, how the
  audit trail and the PM's decisions stay comparable over time, upload formats + validation + confidentiality (AGENTS
  rule 1), and the cost cap for a background agent (D-054/D-055 limits apply).
- Was "Next up" item: background web agent, uploads to the knowledge base, versioning without fixed checkpoints, a job

- Until then the app keeps the per-checkpoint separation (D-055).

- A parallel workstream idea (D-040+): requirement origins (competitors, trends, regulation, personas), a regulatory
  radar, customer & model groups, an offering matrix per market and market intelligence; the information architecture
  would need a home for these. Note: regulation is out of scope for the BMW challenge (AGENTS rule 2).
